reason: Both describe the identical mechanism: is_near_duplicate uses <= instead of >= when comparing cosine similarity to the threshold, causing the classification to invert — near-identical/high-similarity embeddings are misclassified as not-duplicates while dissimilar/orthogonal (low-similarity) embeddings are misclassified as duplicates. The reviewer's finding is a faithful paraphrase of the ground truth's runtime misbehavior, not a different bug or vague complaint.
